subject: Mathematics
central_question: How do geometric locus definitions and cone intersections lead to the standard equations and properties of circles, parabolas, ellipses, and hyperbolas?
in_scope_units: Sections of a double-napped right circular cone.
Circle, ellipse, parabola, and hyperbola from cutting-plane angles.
Degenerate conic sections at the vertex.
Circle definition, equation, centre, radius, and completing squares.
Parabola definition, standard equations, focus, directrix, axis, and latus rectum.
Ellipse definition, axis relation, eccentricity, standard equations, axes, foci, vertices, and latus rectum.
Hyperbola definition, axis relation, eccentricity, standard equations, axes, foci, vertices, and latus rectum.
Applications and locus problems involving mirrors, arches, beams, rods, and flag posts.
banned_topics: Translated or rotated conics with arbitrary centres or axes, which the chapter states are beyond scope.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every plane section of a cone is non-degenerate.
known_pitfalls.correction: A plane through the vertex may produce a point, line, or pair of intersecting lines.

known_pitfalls.claim: The coefficient in y²=4ax equals a.
For an ellipse, a is always under x².
known_pitfalls.correction: a is the semi-major axis and is associated with the larger denominator.

known_pitfalls.claim: Ellipse and hyperbola both satisfy c²=a²−b².

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Section 10.2 for classification of cone sections.
NCERT Example 3 for completing squares in a circle.
NCERT Example 5 for reading parabola parameters.
NCERT Examples 14 and 17 for hyperbola parameters and a parabolic-mirror application.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter contains Exercises 10.1, 10.2, 10.3, and 10.4 followed by the Miscellaneous Exercise on Chapter 10.
